historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (+5.2% 5yr / +5.5% 3yr) diverges sharply from revenue (-0.4% / -13.5%) and EPS (-4.3% / -24.6%): book value kept compounding through retained earnings while the FY2025 VBP shock cut revenue 27.8% and profit 55.6%. The equity CAGR overstates organic growth; the base path uses a rebound-then-fade revenue path below it.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; only FY2021 carried SBC, 67.05). FCF is volatile on working-capital swings (FY2019 -190, FY2024 -49), so the 5yr +10.4% reflects a weak FY2020 base, not a trend. EPS from Metrics.csv (HKD per share).

scenario_narratives.base: FY2025 was the VBP trough, not a new run-rate. Infusion volumes keep growing (H1 2026 +21.4%) on 12th-batch National Centralised Procurement wins and a gradual shift toward therapeutic infusions (peritoneal dialysis, hemofiltration), while oral preparations and APIs stay soft. Tender prices stabilise rather than recover, so EBITDA margin settles at 28.5% -- about 3pp below FY2023 and far below the 33-36% of FY2018-19. Revenue regains FY2024's level only around FY2030. The capex cycle is past its peak, so cash conversion improves, but receivables-heavy working capital keeps absorbing 40 cents of every incremental revenue dollar.
scenario_narratives.bull: The H1 2026 inflection proves durable: higher-value infusions, complex formulations (emulsion, liposome) and the new lyophilized/sterile-powder lines lift mix, export registrations (513 certificates in ~100 countries, CE/WHO-PQ/FDA pursuits) compound, and tender pricing firms as the market consolidates around the CR4. EBITDA margin climbs back to 31% (still below FY2023's 31.6%) and growth runs mid-single-digit for five years. This is roughly the path implied by the HK$3.6-5.0 broker targets.
scenario_narratives.bear: VBP rounds keep compressing price on a widening share of the portfolio. The H1 2026 rebound fades in H2 as provincial alliance tenders re-price infusion solutions; ampoules keep exiting tenders and caffeine exports stay depressed by US tariffs; DRG/DIP hospital cost control squeezes volumes. Revenue falls again in FY2027-28 and margin erodes to 23.5% as the mix shifts further toward tender-won commodity saline and glucose, with capex held near D&A just to keep GMP lines current. A repeat of the 2024 tender-compliance suspension is the tail inside this case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a China IV-infusion and generic-drug maker whose economics are set by the state tender system. The value question is where margins settle after the FY2025 VBP shock, and how much cash receivables-heavy working capital keeps absorbing. Terminal value is capped at 12x FCF, a structurally-slow-business multiple, because Gordon at 8.5%/2% (~15.7x) would capitalise a tender-exposed generic franchise at a premium multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: VBP / National Centralised Procurement re-pricing: each new batch or provincial alliance tender can reset price on a large share of revenue
Working-capital absorption: hospital receivables swung HK$965m in FY2024; the -40% capture assumption is the main gap between EBITDA and cash
Margin settle-point: each 1pp of terminal EBITDA margin is worth roughly 5% of base value
Related-party governance with Sichuan Kelun (~23% holder and the dominant competitor)
RMB/HKD translation: flows are RMB and translated to HKD; a weaker RMB lowers the HKD value one-for-one
Tender-compliance risk: a repeat of the 2024 six-month procurement suspension

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.01-3.18
data_sources.financials: 2005.HK_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2018-FY2025, H1 2024-2026); FY2025 annual report (income statement, cash flow statement, note 20(b) cash-from-operations reconciliation); H1 2026 interim report (balance sheet at 30 Jun 2026, note 7 EPS, note 14 treasury and RSA shares)

inputs.share_count_basis: 2,951,113,385 shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 less 59,670,000 treasury shares (46.2m bought back in FY2025 + 13.47m in H1 2026, of which 8.98m held by the Restricted Share Award trust); H1 2026 interim note 7(b): no dilutive potential ordinary shares. Held FLAT: buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the RSA trust shares, if ever granted, are covered by the 0.2%-of-revenue SBC charge.
inputs.net_debt_note: 30 Jun 2026 interim balance sheet: borrowings 1,855.970 current + 2,185.507 non-current = 4,041.477, plus lease liabilities 2.543 + 4.947 = 7.490 (treatment A, leases as debt) = 4,048.967 total debt. Cash = cash & equivalents 1,855.702 + pledged bank and time deposits 82.753 + 0.432 + trading securities 34.913 = 1,973.800. Finance income is outside profit from operations, so nothing needs stripping from the flows.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 operating cash flow 635.035 less capex 335.256 (PPE 141.057 + right-of-use/land 30.516 + intangible additions 163.683), FY2025 AR cash flow statement line 5309-5318. Post interest paid (109.0) and tax paid (108.2); before government grants received (94.5, not credited in the forward build).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: no equity-settled share-based payment expense in FY2022-FY2025 (last charge HK$67.05m in FY2021, note 6(b)). No net-share-settlement withholding (HK). Forward path carries 0.2% of revenue for future Restricted Share Award grants (trust bought 8.98m shares for HK$19.9m in H1 2026; 8-year average expense ~HK$8m/yr).
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 payments for repurchase of own shares HK$154.4m (financing activities), H1 2026 HK$55.2m. The flat count is being funded by a genuine repurchaser.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are economically RMB (substantially all revenue and 82% of borrowings are RMB) translated to HKD. CoE ~9.7%: China 10y ~1.9% + ERP ~6.5% x beta ~0.95 + ~1.5% HK small-cap/listing premium. Pre-tax cost of debt ~3.3% (mostly onshore variable RMB loans), ~2.8% after tax. Market weights ~79% equity (mkt cap ~HK$7.95bn) / 21% net debt -> ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. VBP/tender risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not as a WACC premium; WACC identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): lease liabilities (HK$7.5m) in net debt; principal not deducted from flows. Land-use-right purchases (HK$30.5m FY2025) sit inside capex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book (HK$335.0m at 30 Jun 2026). NCI share of profit is ~2.7% of attributable (FY2025 12.8 vs 470.6), so book is a reasonable proxy.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'. SSY is a manufacturing operating company (IV infusion, ampoules, oral preps, APIs, medical materials) -- not a financial, REIT or holdco -- so free cash flow is the right stream. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). EBITDA = profit from operations + depreciation + amortisation (FY2025 628.9 + 372.7 + 80.8 = 1,082.4), excluding share of associate profit (associate added at book in the bridge) and finance income/costs. EBITDA includes ~HK$32m/yr non-cash amortisation of deferred government grants, while grant cash receipts (HK$94m FY2025) are not credited -- a small conservative offset. Working capital is a heavy drain for a China hospital supplier (receivables + inventory - payables - contract liabilities ~55% of annualised H1 2026 revenue; FY2024 receivables rose HK$965m), so wc_capture is -40% of the revenue change. SBC-light market: house and street differ only by the 0.2% RSA charge. The declared H1 2026 interim dividend (HK$0.055/sh, ~HK$159m) is not yet a liability on the 30 Jun balance sheet and is not deducted. Analysis.json is currently malformed JSON (line 81) -- read as text; flag for the qualitative-analyst.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 +8.5%: H1 2026 HK$2,361m (+9.9%, ~5% in RMB) plus H2 2025 base HK$2,018m grown ~7% gives ~HK$4,520m. Then fade to 2.5% as VBP price erosion offsets infusion volume and export growth.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: H1 2026 EBITDA margin 28.6% (674.4/2,360.6); H2 is seasonally weaker (H2 2025 23.8%, H2 2024 29.5%), so FY2026 ~27.4%. Recovers to 28.5% on stabilising tender prices and mix, well below FY2023's 31.6% and FY2018-19's 33-36%.
base.da_capex_rationale: D&A HK$453m in FY2025 (10.9%) is roughly flat in dollars as the capex cycle passes its peak (commitments HK$318m vs HK$562m a year earlier), so it falls as a % of revenue; capex 8.0% (FY2025 actual) glides to 7.5%, at or just above D&A at maturity.
base.cash_tax_rationale: Effective tax 14.2% FY2025, 16.1% FY2024, 15.7% H1 2026 (high-tech enterprise 15% on the main PRC subsidiaries, 25% elsewhere); 16.5% allows for PRC dividend withholding on upstreamed profits.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because revenue depends on a single policy channel (National Centralised Procurement / provincial VBP) that cut revenue 27.8% in one year, and the 2024 suspension shows compliance fragility. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs mix shift, export certification and tender-price recovery to go right together. Base holds 50%: the H1 2026 recovery and the 12th-batch wins are evidence, but one half-year is not a trend.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
